purpose: Maps each question generator to the source material that supports the README's TMUA no-calculator fluency claim.

claimLevels.official-direct: The generator directly drills a named topic or skill in the TMUA specification or Notes on Logic and Proof.
claimLevels.official-adjacent: The generator drills a narrow fluency move used inside a named TMUA topic, but the exact micro-drill is not itself named.
claimLevels.fluency-support: The generator supports no-calculator speed or prerequisite fluency, but should not be presented as a direct TMUA syllabus item.

sources.notes: Used for local source mapping of test structure, Section 1 mathematics content, and Section 2 Paper 2 logic/proof scope.

sources.path: tmua papers/TMUA Notes on Logic and Proof 2021.pdf
sources.notes: Used for the logic generator mapping: necessary/sufficient, converse/contrapositive, quantifiers, negation, and counterexample/disproof patterns.

Quadratic functions; solution of quadratic equations; factorise quadratics.
Completing the square.
The discriminant of a quadratic function.
Derive a formula, substitute into a formula.
Use of the Factor Theorem and the Remainder Theorem.
Simultaneous equations: analytical solution by substitution; set up and solve linear equations including simultaneous equations in two unknowns.
Solution of linear and quadratic inequalities.
Familiarity with f(x)=|x| and the modulus function graph.
Laws of indices; use index laws to simplify, multiply, and divide powers.
The solution of equations of the form a^x=b, and equations reducible to this form.
Definition and laws of logarithms, including log_a a = 1.
Values of sine, cosine, and tangent for 0, 30, 45, 60, and 90 degrees.
Trigonometric functions, symmetries, identities, and simple equations; the exact double-angle micro-drill supports these but is not named as a formula requirement.
Knowledge and use of tan(theta)=sin(theta)/cos(theta) and sin^2(theta)+cos^2(theta)=1.
The sine and cosine rules.
The area of a triangle in the form 1/2 ab sin C.
Solution of simple trigonometric equations in a given interval.
Sine, cosine, and tangent functions; graphs, symmetries, and periodicity.
Cartesian coordinates and Pythagoras; distance formula fluency supports coordinate geometry.
Coordinate geometry in the (x,y) plane; midpoint is supporting coordinate fluency.
Conditions for two straight lines to be parallel or perpendicular; gradients of parallel and perpendicular lines.
Equation of a straight line and finding equations of straight lines given information in various forms.
Coordinate geometry of the circle using (x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2 and x^2+y^2+cx+dy+e=0.
Derivative as gradient and differentiation of x^n for rational n and related sums/differences.
Definite integration, integrating powers, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
Approximation of the area under a curve using the trapezium rule.
Applications of differentiation to stationary points and using differentiation to determine graph shape.
Arithmetic series, including the formula for the sum of the first n natural numbers.
Sequences generated by a simple recurrence relation of the form x_{n+1}=f(x_n).
The sum of a finite geometric series.
The sum to infinity of a convergent geometric series, including |r|<1.
Compositions of transformations and familiarity with function mappings.
Familiarity with f(x)=|x| and the modulus function.
Use Pythagoras' theorem in 2-dimensions and 3-dimensions.
Find circumferences and areas of circles, including arcs, segments and sectors.
Radian measure, including use for arc length and area of sector and segment; circles including arcs, segments and sectors.
Calculate and use the sums of the interior and exterior angles of polygons.
Differentiation of x^n for rational n and related sums and differences.
Binomial expansion and coefficient notation.
Surds and solution of quadratic equations.
Use and manipulation of surds; denesting is a stronger fluency extension rather than a named requirement.
Logarithm laws and exact log evaluation; the 2021 specification says questions requiring the change-of-base formula will not be set, so this generator should be treated as adjacent fluency only.
Laws of logarithms for combining sums, differences, and multiples of logs.
Coordinate geometry of the circle using general and centre-radius forms.
Modulus function familiarity and area fluency; area of |x|+|y|=k is not named directly.
Linear inequalities and familiarity with f(x)=|x|; exact modulus inequality comparison is adjacent.
Percentage, ratio, and proportion fluency; weighted-average mixtures are supporting no-calculator practice rather than a named generator target.
Order, add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions.
Understand and use the terms necessary and sufficient.
A is sufficient for B means if A then B; A is necessary for B means if B then A.
The converse and contrapositive of a statement; relationship between a statement and its converse/contrapositive.
Converse and contrapositive of if A then B.
Use for all, for some, and there exists; negate statements using these terms.
not-(for all) is equivalent to (there exists) not; not-(there exists) is equivalent to (for all) not.
Disproof by counterexample.
A counterexample to if A then B is an example where A is true and B is false.

claimBoundaries: This map supports the README claim that the app drills broad TMUA no-calculator recall and fluency.
It does not support a claim that the app is complete TMUA preparation.
It does not claim to model full multi-step MCQs or a complete Paper 2 proof course.
